title: DecompGAIL: Learning Realistic Traffic Behaviors with Decomposed Multi-Agent Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
claim: A holistic discriminator penalizes good ego behavior because of misbehaving neighbors; decomposing realism into separate components avoids this conflicting reward.
layout: 2 panels split by dotted line, left-to-right flow, dashed decomposition arrows into summed rewards
description: Two side-by-side panels separated by a vertical dotted line. Panel (a), Decentralized GAIL, shows a small top-down road scene of yellow, green and red cars inside a dashed red circle around the ego car. A solid arrow labeled Discriminator leads to Fake, then down to Low Reward. A second arrow runs from the ego car down to Realistic Behavior. Two opposing arrows between Realistic Behavior and Low Reward are labeled Conflict. Panel (b), Decomposed GAIL, starts with the same road scene. Dashed arrows labeled Decompose split it into three parts: ego with the map, ego alone, and ego with neighbors. Each part has an arrow to Real. The Real outputs feed a circled-plus node that sums them into a final reward. The eye goes first to the red dashed circle and the Conflict arrows.
caption: Comparison with standard decentralized GAIL. (a) A standard decentralized discriminator evaluating local observations can yield spuriously low rewards for ego-realistic behavior due to unrealistic neighbor–neighbor interactions. (b) DecompGAIL separately assesses ego–map and ego–neighbor realism, combining them to obtain a high reward for expert-like ego behavior even when neighbors misbehave.
abstract: Realistic traffic simulation is critical for the development of autonomous driving systems and urban mobility planning, yet existing imitation learning approaches often fail to model realistic traffic behaviors. Behavior cloning suffers from covariate shift, while Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (GAIL) is notoriously unstable in multi-agent settings. We identify a key source of this instability: irrelevant interaction misguidance, where a discriminator penalizes an ego vehicle's realistic behavior due to unrealistic interactions among its neighbors. To address this, we propose Decomposed Multi-agent GAIL (DecompGAIL), which explicitly decomposes realism into ego-map and ego-neighbor components, filtering out misleading neighbor: neighbor and neighbor: map interactions. We further introduce a social PPO objective that augments ego rewards with distance-weighted neighborhood rewards, encouraging overall realism across agents. Integrated into a lightweight SMART-based backbone, DecompGAIL achieves state-of-the-art performance on the WOMD Sim Agents 2025 benchmark.
